## About the course

**MP223 Applied Econometric Methods for the Social Sciences** was taught at JLU
Giessen in Summer Semester 2022. It introduces regression analysis as a tool for
causal reasoning, taught entirely through R: every method on the slides is
immediately practised on real data in a matching application exercise.

The course covers seven topics — [introduction and research
design](topics/00-introduction.qmd), [data wrangling](topics/10-data-wrangling.qmd),
[describing data](topics/20-data-description.qmd), [simple
regression](topics/30-simple-regression.qmd), [multiple
regression](topics/40-multiple-regression.qmd), [panel
regression](topics/50-panel-regression.qmd) and [instrumental
variables](topics/60-instrumental-variables.qmd).

## Reusing these materials

The materials are published openly so that students can revisit them after the
course and so that other instructors can build on them. The
[repository](https://github.com/EBukin/mp223-2022-aem-R-public/) contains every
source file — `.qmd` decks, `.Rmd` exercises and the data they use.

If you reuse or adapt them, please credit **Eduard Bukin** and link back to
[ebukin.github.io](https://ebukin.github.io).

## Colophon

Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/). Slides are
[revealjs](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/) decks; exercises are
R Markdown documents rendered to HTML. Everything is deployed automatically from
the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/EBukin/mp223-2022-aem-R-public/).
